stumbles.why: Unclear what 'caps' means at first (capitalized emphasis like NEVER in instructions); only inferred later from the baby honey example.

stumbles.quote: 42/43 violations in every form, even with no directive
stumbles.why: Unclear what is being counted: 42 of 43 what? Trials? 'Every form' of what (phrasing variants)? 'Violations' of what rule is never stated.

stumbles.quote: Naming a forbidden word raised its log-odds ~2.5.
stumbles.why: Unclear whose log-odds (the model's probability of producing the word) and relative to what baseline; seems to conflict with 'no difference' unless naming differs from caps.
Not explained what the directive is or what task the model was given; it is unclear how a violation can occur with no rule.

stumbles.quote: Its 22,100-doc corpus had one caps instruction
stumbles.why: Unclear what 'its' refers to (the model's training corpus) and how this relates to the finding; the implied explanation (model never learned caps emphasis) is left unstated.

point: A tiny model (Baguettotron, 321M) ignored all-caps emphasis in instructions, likely because its training data had almost none, and merely naming a forbidden word made it more likely to produce it.
